title: Rehab and prosthesis after amputation
also: learning to walk with a prosthetic leg
what: After an amputation, the residual limb is prepared for a prosthesis, and then you are taught to walk and live with it. A doctor, a prosthetist, and a rehab specialist work together.
why: After a leg or arm amputation, once the wound has healed and your doctor allows it.
duration: a session usually takes 45 to 60 minutes; getting to confident walking usually takes months
tell_doctor: How the residual limb is healing and whether it hurts
Phantom pain, a feeling of pain in the missing part
What you did before the amputation: work, hobbies
How your home is set up: stairs, bathroom

prepare.title: Residual limb
prepare.text: Bandaging or a silicone liner helps shape the limb. A specialist will show you how.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Check the skin of the residual limb every day and keep it clean and dry.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, shorts or loose trousers, and a shoe for your healthy foot.

bring: Your prosthesis, if you already have one
steps: The doctor examines the residual limb and your general condition
You do exercises for strength and joint movement
The prosthetist takes measurements and makes the prosthesis
You learn to put it on and take it off
You practice standing and walking with it, at first by parallel bars
Then you learn stairs and walking outdoors
feel: Walking on the prosthesis is hard and tiring at first
Phantom sensations and pain are common, so tell your doctor
The residual limb may rub, especially at the start
after: Check the skin of the residual limb every day
If the prosthesis rubs, do not put up with it, show it to the prosthetist
The prosthesis is adjusted over time, since the limb changes
red_flags: A sore, redness, or pus on the residual limb
The limb turned blue, is cold, or hurts sharply
You fell and hit yourself hard

faq.q: When can I put on a prosthesis?
faq.a: Usually once the wound has healed, after a few weeks. Your doctor will tell you the time.
Often it gets weaker over time. There are ways to ease it, so tell your doctor.

reminders.text: Rehab session today. Bring your prosthesis, if you have one, and comfortable clothes.
